records.claimDecision: When FreeNet Hub Full-System is active, update and node retrieval bind to the pre-TUN source interface captured before TUN creation and verify that the bound trace is not the post-TUN trace. An external VPN that already owns the system route before FreeNet Hub remains part of that base route.
Official gateway_request StartPc WARP, system speed, update-during-tunnel base-route binding, Stop, and route restoration all passed on the installed R37 payload.

Direct speed test bypasses FreeNet Hub browser proxy and fails closed if the default route is not a trusted physical route or Cloudflare reports WARP/Gateway. Installed live sample used Ethernet 3 and measured 78.3 ms / 37.71 Mbps / 5.23 Mbps.
Installed R37 app and gateway trees match current source manifests exactly (17 app files + 17 gateway files, zero mismatches). Self-contained runtime bootstrap passed.
Public-tree security scan passes with zero forbidden runtime artifacts and zero sensitive-pattern hits after removing hardcoded user paths from test harnesses.

Direct-DPI remains an optional extension rather than a main-product promotion gate. Live direct and Chrome evidence pass, but an installed lifecycle-specific acceptance is still unproven; therefore it stays fail-closed optional.

R37 Final installer rebuilt with canonical public-release metadata and installed successfully. Exact final build passed installer exit, runtime bootstrap, source/install parity, five-tab smoke and route preservation.

records.context: Final metadata promotion on installed runtime
records.claimDecision: Installed app manifest and RELEASE metadata were promoted to R37 Final with automatic backups only after runtime acceptance; post-promotion 17+17 manifest parity and five-tab smoke passed with route unchanged.

Because the connected execution environment would not launch the final EXE, an exact owner-run verification runner was prepared. It hash-pins the R37 Final installer, backs up the current install, runs silent install, verifies runtime bootstrap, release revision, manifest parity, five-tab smoke and route preservation, and restores the backup on failure.

RELEASE source hashes use canonical Git-filtered bytes for public verification, while app/gateway runtime manifests continue to use raw deployed-byte hashes. Final metadata installer acceptance passed.

The exact public candidate passes canonical PUBLIC_MANIFEST verification, app/gateway/cross-platform/windows package manifests, canonical RELEASE hashes, forbidden-runtime guard, security scan, broad regression and git diff check.

Runtime integrity and source-checkout integrity use separate hashes. app manifest `sha256` remains exact deployed-byte hash consumed by FreeNetHub.ps1; new `sourceSha256` records canonical Git-filtered bytes consumed by verify_public_tree.py. This prevents LF/CRLF checkout normalization from weakening runtime integrity or causing false CI failures.

R37 was published as the latest GitHub release at tag v4.2.0-r37-final targeting commit 45e21a1bc64aefaf3276751754c0f4f4fd1fb649. Hosted CI #99 passed all jobs. Release asset digests match local accepted artifacts, and installed post-publish UpdateCheck selects the R37 asset but correctly reports updateAvailable=false because local and remote revisions are both 37.

Linux 4.2.0-linux.9-r37 replaces the old five-page Linux UI with the accepted R37 product architecture (Dashboard, Methods, Nodes, Tools, Settings) and connects it to a Linux-native parity backend. Node Pool reuses the same nodehub parser/config generator semantics as Windows. Node refresh fetch/parse/merge is separated from explicit Test All, and real proxy health remains distinct from TCP endpoint reachability and throughput completeness.

Linux Node Pool provisions app-local sing-box 1.14.2 from the official SagerNet release only after archive SHA-256 verification. Installed binary integrity is rechecked at runtime. No system-wide package install is required.

Linux R9 exact ZIP payload installed on aliemad-Labtop with internal SHA256SUMS PASS, installed integrity PASS, GTK process restart, exact route preservation including pre-existing external tun0, and no auto-connect. Browser WARP/GOOL/CFON are real hash-pinned warp-plus paths; Node Pool uses hash-pinned sing-box. Node endpoint reachability and real HTTPS proxy health remain separate gates.

records.context: Linux R9 feature-complete R37 UI surface
records.claimDecision: Linux R9 exposes Dashboard, Methods, Nodes, Tools and Settings with method connect/benchmark, Node URL/file/clipboard import, explicit Test All, bounded benchmark, sort/filter, favorite/pin, editable metadata, history, Raw/Base64 export, revision-aware update check/install, diagnostics, Console and Tor/bridges. Full-System Node remains explicitly unclaimed without a separately accepted privileged helper.

FreeNetHub_4.2.0_Linux_R9.zip exact current superset package passed internal SHA256SUMS, exact install, UI restart, installed integrity, py_compile and route preservation. Earlier EF609D package is superseded by the final current-authority package.

Dashboard pre-connect testing honors Settings: BASE binds to the physical base interface and does not enter either a pre-existing tun0 or the selected provider; SELECTED benchmarks the selected provider. With external tun0 active and WARP selected, BASE produced IR/warp=off on enp1s0 with Ping 291.1 ms, Download 17.53 Mbps and Upload 4.55 Mbps, and routes were unchanged.

The exact deterministic Linux R9 ZIP was extracted into a fresh temporary HOME and installed from its payload. Internal PACKAGE_MANIFEST, both upstream archive pins, installed INSTALL.sha256, source/install parity and route preservation all passed; install performed no network-route mutation.

The Linux CI job was extended so a green hosted run must compile the R37 parity backend and shared node parser, run the R37 parity regression, syntax-check both pinned dependency installers, and deterministically build the R9 ZIP. The prior Linux CI surface was insufficient for R9 promotion.
